item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 121154
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 AM PDT Mon Oct 12 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Simon, centered about 50 miles off the coast of Cabo Corrientes,
Mexico.

South of Southern Mexico (EP93):
A broad area of low pressure located several hundred miles
south-southwest of the coast of Guatemala continues to produce
disorganized showers and thunderstorms. This system is gradually
becoming better defined, and environmental conditions are forecast
to be conducive for further development. A tropical depression is
expected to form well south of southern Mexico in the next two days
while the system moves generally west-northwestward at around 10
mph.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...80 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

$$
Forecaster Hagen

item.title: Hurricane Simon Public Advisory Number 21
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM MST Mon Oct 12 2026 
ZCZC MIATCPEP5 ALL
TTAA00 KNHC DDHHMM
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Simon Advisory Number  21
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
800 AM MST Mon Oct 12 2026
 
...SIMON CONTINUES MOVING SLOWLY NORTHWESTWARD OFFSHORE OF MEXICO...
...DANGEROUS WINDS EXPECTED FOR A FEW MORE HOURS WITH FLOODING RAINS
TO CONTINUE ALONG THE COAST...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 AM MST...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...20.1N 106.5W
ABOUT 55 MI...90 KM WSW OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
ABOUT 215 MI...345 KM S OF MAZATLAN MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...110 MPH...175 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 315 DEGREES AT 3 MPH...6 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...962 MB...28.41 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
The government of Mexico has changed the Hurricane Warning to a
Hurricane Watch from north of Cabo Corrientes to El Roblito.
 
The government of Mexico has changed the Hurricane Warning to a
Tropical Storm Warning from Playa Perula north to Cabo Corrientes.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Hurricane Warning is in effect for...
* Las Islas Marias
 
A Hurricane Watch is in effect for...
* North of Cabo Corrientes to Bahia Tempehuaya
 
A Tropical Storm Warning in in effect for...
* Playa Perula to Cabo Corrientes
 
A Hurricane Warning means that hurricane conditions are expected
somewhere within the warning area. Preparations to protect life
and property should be rushed to completion.
 
A Hurricane Watch means that hurricane conditions are possible
within the watch area within 48 hours.
 
A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
expected somewhere within the warning area, in this cast for the
next few hours.
 
Interests elsewhere in west-central Mexico should continue to
monitor as changes to watches and warnings are possible later today.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 AM MST (1500 UTC), the center of Hurricane Simon was located
near latitude 20.1 North, longitude 106.5 West. Simon is moving
toward the northwest near 3 mph (6 km/h) and this general
motion is expected to continue into early Tuesday. A gradual turn
toward the northeast is forecast thereafter, and Simon is expected
to approach the west-central Mexico coastline on Wednesday into
Thursday.
 
Maximum sustained winds have decreased to near 110 mph (175 km/h)
with higher gusts. Some additional weakening is forecast today, but
Simon could re-intensify some on Tuesday and Wednesday and is
expected to remain a hurricane through midweek. Rapid weakening is
likely after Simon moves inland late this week.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 15 miles (30 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 60 miles
(95 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 962 mb (28.41 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Simon can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP5 and WMO header WTPZ45 KNHC.
 
WIND: Hurricane conditions are likely to occur in the Hurricane
Warning area of Las Islas Marias. Tropical storm conditions are
expected to occur for a few more hours in the Tropical Storm warning
area. Hurricane conditions are possible within the watch area by
Wednesday, with tropical storm conditions possible by Tuesday night.
 
RAINFALL: Simon is expected to produce additional rainfall totals of
2 to 4 inches across coastal portions of southwest and west-central
Mexico with isolated additional amounts of 6 to 8 inches over
portions of the state of Jalisco through early this week, and the
state of Sinaloa mainly Wednesday and Thursday. Isolated maximum
storm totals of 30 inches are possible over portions of the states
of Michoacan, Colima, and Jalisco.  This rainfall will produce
life-threatening flooding and mudslides or worsen any on-going
flooding, especially in areas of steep terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Simon,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep5.shtml?rainqpf.
 
STORM SURGE: A dangerous storm surge is expected along the immediate
coast near and to the east of where the center approaches land. Near
the coast, the surge will be accompanied by large and destructive
waves.
 
SURF:  Swells generated by Simon will affect portions of the coast
of southwestern and west-central Mexico during the next few days.
These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip
current conditions. Please consult products from your local weather
office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next intermediate advisory at 1100 AM MST.
Next complete advisory at 200 PM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Papin
 
NNNN

item.title: Hurricane Simon Forecast Discussion Number 20
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM MST Mon Oct 12 2026 
000
WTPZ45 KNHC 120854
TCDEP5
 
Hurricane Simon Discussion Number  20
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
200 AM MST Mon Oct 12 2026
 
Simon continues to show signs of weakening as the eye has become
filled in, although infrared imagery shows that the central dense 
overcast has cooled since the previous advisory. There is a wide 
spread in intensity estimates, ranging from 73-127 kt. Since there 
has been an overall modest degradation to the cloud pattern, the 
current intensity is nudged downward to 100 kt. The initial wind 
radii were modified with the help of timely SAR pass.
 
The cyclone is drifting off to the northwest as it is being steered 
by a distant mid-level ridge centered over the south-central United 
States. Simon is expected to continue moving slowly near the coast 
of Mexico for the next few days. However, there is still a higher 
than normal amount of uncertainty in the track, and some models 
show that Simon gets trapped in an area of light steering between 
the US ridge and one well southwest of Simon. Later, a trough from 
the northwest will approach the hurricane and force Simon to turn 
toward the northeast with increasing forward speed, though the 
timing of this turn is uncertain. The latest NHC forecast is just 
west of the previous advisory after considering some of the latest 
AI-based guidance.  
 
Weakening is expected to continue due to Simon's proximity to the 
mountainous terrain, as well as some easterly wind shear. However, 
the sea-surface temperatures that Simon will be moving across 
later this week are around 31-32 C, which could moderate the 
weakening trend, as well as the new track being slightly farther 
offshore. The current NHC intensity forecast is generally the same 
as the previous forecast with only a few adjustments. Simon is 
still expected to rapidly weakening once the cyclone makes landfall 
around 72 h.

 
Key Messages:
 
1. Dangerous wind and storm surge impacts are likely along a 
portion of the west-central coast of Mexico, and a Hurricane 
Warning is in effect from Playa Perula to El Roblito. Residents 
should continue to shelter in a safe room to ride out the
storm as the most significant hazards are ongoing.
 
2. Simon is expected to approach the coast of western Mexico later
this week, where hurricane conditions are possible. A Hurricane
Watch is in effect from El Roblito to Bahia Tempehuaya.
 
3. Heavy rainfall associated with Simon will impact portions of 
southwestern and west-central Mexico over the next few days. This 
rainfall will produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides, 
especially in areas of steep terrain.
 
4. Large swells will affect portions of the southwestern and 
west-central coasts of Mexico over the next few days. These swells 
are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip current 
conditions. Please consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
